calcite,thenthemarblewilllikelybewhite(asinFigure7.10),butifithadvariousimpurities,suchasclay,silica,

Quartzite is metamorphosed sandstone (Figure 7.11). It is dominated by quartz, and in many cases, the original
quartz grains of the sandstone are welded together with additional silica. Most sandstone contains some clay
minerals andmayalsoinclude otherminerals suchasfeldsparorfragments ofrock,somostquartzite hassome
impurities with the quartz.
Evenifformedduring regional metamorphism,quartzitedoesnottendtobefoliatedbecausequartzcrystalsdon’t
align with the directional pressure. On the other hand, any clay present in the original sandstone is likely to be
converted to mica during metamorphism, and any such mica is likely to align with the directional pressure. An
example of this is shown in Figure 7.12. The quartz crystals show no alignment, but the micas are all aligned,
indicating that there was directional pressure during regional metamorphism of this rock.
